title: Abstract DP168: Chronic Stroke Plasma Triggers Microglial Activation and Cognitive Decline in Young Mice

evidence_spans.quote: Methods: Blood plasma was collected from aged (18-month-old) male and female C57Bl/6 mice
healthy young recipient mice
Increased gliosis and senescent-like phenotypes were confirmed using immunohistochemistry.
Our ongoing work aims to identify the molecular mediators of these effects through multi-omic profiling.

scope_reviewer.concise_rationale: This empirical mouse experiment reports a senescent-like phenotype, but multi-omic profiling is stated only as ongoing future work; the current report describes non-omics phenotyping rather than two molecular omics layers.

causal_design_reviewer.comparator: Infusion of plasma from sham-surgery donor mice
causal_design_reviewer.outcome: Recognition and associative memory impairment; microglial activation and related brain inflammatory/senescence markers
causal_design_reviewer.estimand_or_contrast: Outcomes in young recipients infused with chronic-stroke plasma versus sham plasma
